column1: # doctest-ignore-baseline.tsv — the exemption ledger for `scripts/check-bare-ignore.py --fences`.
# Format:  kind <TAB> path <TAB> key <TAB> note
#   kind    `no-reason`  a ```ignore fence with no `// IGNORED: …` first line
#           `inert-attr` an info-string mixing a doctest attribute with a token rustdoc
#                        does not know, which silently makes the block not-a-doctest
#   key     the first 12 hex of sha1(path + "\n" + the fence body, blank lines dropped).
#           It is keyed on the BODY, not the line, so a row survives the file moving
#           around the fence and DIES when the example itself is rewritten. Two fences
#           with an identical body in the same file share a key; one row covers both.
#           `scripts/check-bare-ignore.py --report-fences` prints the key.
# ⚠ THIS FILE RATCHETS. A row that matches nothing is a FAILURE, not a shrug: a repaired
# fence has to retire its own exemption in the same commit. Otherwise the file decays
# into a list of things that used to be wrong and nobody can tell which are which.
# There is deliberately NO regenerate flag. Adding a row is supposed to cost a sentence.
# Seeded 2026-07-27, from the pass that repaired 45 of the 71 ```ignore fences this tree
# had (and re-marked the rest ```text / ```no_run / ```ignore-with-a-reason). Everything
# below is remainder this pass could not honestly touch — NOT remainder it gave up on.
# UPSTREAM, not ours to author. `deos-homeserver/vendor/askama_derive` is a vendored copy
# of the askama proc-macro crate; these four fences are upstream's own doc examples of
# template syntax inside `#[derive(Template)]`. Repairing them would mean diverging a
# vendored crate from upstream to satisfy a house convention. If the vendor drop is ever
# refreshed and these move, the keys change and these rows go stale — which is correct:
# re-read them then, do not re-baseline them blind.
